question: Which of the following objectives is NOT a part of watershed management?

options.text: Restoring water levels in downstream rivers

solution:
The correct answer is __**Generating electricity.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The** watershed** is the area of land that drains or sheds water into a specific receiving water body, such as a lake or a river.
 
• In the **watershed,** as rainwater or melted snow flows downward, silt and other elements are** **__picked up, transported, and dumped into the receiving waterbody.
 
• **A** **comprehensive** watershed **plan** **must** first identify the characteristics of the watershed and **develop **the watershed's natural resources.
 
• To properly plan and actually measure improvements in watershed resources,** **it is important to establish a baseline for the **type** and quality of the **entire** **watershed.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__****

 
• **Watershed Management?****​**

 
 
• **Basin** management refers to the **improvement** **of** **land** **use practices** **and** **water** **management** **by managing** **the** **use** **of** **land and** **water** **resources** **within** **river** **basins** in a **comprehensive manner** **in** **order to** **protect** **and** **improve** **the** **quality** **of** these resources**.** A term used to describe the process of **enforcing **a **practice** **m****anaged.**
 
• Runoff from **rainwater **and **snowmelt** can **lead** **to** **large** amounts of pollution **in** **lakes** **and** **rivers.** Watershed management **reduces **pollution of **watersheds** and other natural resources by identifying the different **types** of pollution present in **watersheds** **and** the **transport of** **these** pollutants and recommending ways to reduce or eliminate **these** **sources** **of** **pollution.**
 
 
 
• Water resource management is the activity of planning, developing, distributing, and managing the optimum use of water resources. It is a sub-set of water cycle management.
 
• Water scarcity can be overcome through proper management of available water, which aids in water conservation and reduces waste. ​
